q: He will only go back to sleep if nursed otherwise he just screams if you try to rock him. He is EBF so husband can’t help. Sometimes it takes an hour or more get him back to sleep.
cx: Nearly nine months; waking three to four times a night since four months.

q: I don’t want to do cry it out but we’ve tried gentler methods and he just screams as soon as you put him into his crib, no matter if he’s exhausted or wide awake.
cx: Gentle options exhausted; CIO refused.

q: I know it’s normal for babies to wake in the night. I was hoping it would be better by now, maybe 1-2 wake-ups. […] I feel like I just can’t do anything right
cx: She already knows the reassurance; expectation not met.

q: Please, if you have any advice or just solidarity I would love to hear it, I feel so alone in this right now.
cx: Asks for company as much as advice.

q: Last night he was awake for two full hours from 2-4AM. Towards the end, I stopped nursing and gave him water and a snack. I then just picked him up and rocked him while he cried, and he finally fell asleep on my chest.
cx: Eighteen-month-old, cosleeping and nursing, suddenly has split nights.

q: It’s helpful to know others are going through it too. Just frustrating that there’s nothing I can do!
cx: Reply to 'it's a phase' comments.

q: the biggest recent change is he started daycare (we are on week 5). […] I wish they’d nap him later because it just feels like a weird schedule.
cx: Daycare's fixed nap leaves a six-hour evening wake window.

q: she has been impossible to put to sleep and I'm terrified to go home from work. I work a half day today, and I literally don't want to go home.
cx: Nine-month-old; mother of two dreads the night ahead.

q: Last night the only way we could get her to go to sleep was to take her for a drive. We took her for THREE DRIVES between 6pm and 6am. This obviously isn't sustainable, but idk what else to do.
cx: Held, fed, sung to, patted; nothing else settled her.

q: What do you do when you can't settle your baby? Just let them cry? We never did CIO with my son (now 3.8), but then, we never had to, he was always able to be settled one way or another.
cx: Second child unlike the first.

q: I do have a husband and we share the load, but there's nowhere in the house where I can't hear her, so I'm up regardless
cx: Shared nights do not help when the house carries the crying.

q: At 4:15am I needed a break. So I told myself I’d set her in her crib in her own room and give myself 3 minutes to regroup. Well I noticed she cried for 20 seconds and started sucking her hand and rubbing her head, no crying. She fell asleep on her own in 5 minutes
cx: First night of the regression; a break for the parent revealed the baby could self-settle.

q: What should I do tonight? Is it silly to try anything when the regression has just started?
cx: Weighing a move to her own room.

q: have to hold his hand/lay with him for up to an hour until he Is asleep enough we can sneak out. And he wakes up multiple times throughout the night, screaming and crying until a parent lays with him.
cx: Two-year-old formerly a good sleeper; says 'scary' at night.

q: The room is very small and there’s not much space between the two single beds for an adult to lay down on the hard floor. The only option is to lay on the single bed with him which is difficult, uncomfortable and makes it hard to leave him without him noticing.
cx: Shares a room with his four-year-old brother.

q: I feel terrible in the morning when I know she probably woke at 3 for a feed and fell back asleep probably hungry because she didn’t cry.
cx: Nearly five-month-old wakes silently; parent sleeps through it.

q: We went to the doc today and they just had a nurse do her shot and I never saw the actual doc. Told me to send my questions on the app they use. Super annoying.
cx: Feeding question about night feeds went unanswered at the visit.

q: He’s calm in my arms, but flips out as soon as it’s dad or the bed that touches him. I’m talking crying to the point of gagging, dry heaving and sometimes actual vomiting.
cx: Eight-month-old; nights fell apart over two weeks.

q: This lack of sleep is changing me for the worse. I’m angry and resentful frequently. I know he’s a little baby and didn’t ask for this but the lack of sleep and inconsistency of it all is really getting to me.
cx: Parent of two, baby almost always held.

q: I struggle to fall sleep because I’m always terrified of the night to come.
cx: Dread of the night itself.

q: I did it at 5.5 months with my oldest and it was tough, but it worked. However, he was much less stubborn than my baby.
cx: Planning to sleep train tonight.

q: His usual schedule is 3/3.25/4.25. I’ve tried more and less time and it always results in the same. He’ll sleep through the night once or twice and then everything goes to shit again.
cx: Schedule tweaks do not change the outcome.

q: I have tried with 11 hours total awake time before and it was a disaster. I kept the schedule for 4-5 days but I gave up after the endless overtired meltdowns…
cx: Reply to a commenter suggesting more awake time.

q: We have tried everything. Sleep sac, warming up bassinet, rubbing smell on it, hand on chest. The longest we have ever gotten her to sleep independently is about 25 minutes.
cx: Three-month-old held for every sleep since birth.

q: I love my baby but I am so extremely burnt out I cry everyday. She starts daycare soon and I worry she will get no sleep.
cx: Daycare start looming.

q: I’m so tired of holding her constantly. My ped did say we could start sleep training at 4 months so gonna try. What method did you use? Did it work?
cx: Doctor's green light sets the start date.

q: There is zero consistency. Sometimes shes hungry, sometimes she rocks back to sleep, sometimes she eats and konks out sometimes she eats and is wide awake. I am EXHAUSTED from the 430-7 am hours and they are MISERABLE.
cx: Second baby, 5.5 months, anchor-nap schedule.

q: We also cannot CIO because we have a toddler and baby is a screamer, so she wakes him up when she screams
cx: Sibling in the house rules out crying methods.

q: Around 13 months he started developing separation anxiety and would scream if I left him. He would escalate so quickly if he did start crying he would immediately throw up. This happened multiple times, every night…so I’ve decided letting him CIO is not going to happen.
cx: Ferber at eight to nine months had worked.

q: For the last two months we are sitting in his room, lights out, while he is in his bed.  This routine takes anywhere from 20-45 min because he will jump and play until he is so exhausted he passes out.
cx: What replaced CIO.

q: he is still in the room with me at night. I have a 6 year old and I’m nervous if I move him into his room my 6 year old won’t sleep
cx: Fifteen-month-old; room arrangements limited by an older sibling.

q: We recently took a short roadtrip and the airbnb did not have a crib, so we ended up cosleeping. Ever since we got back, he expects to sleep on the bed (our biggest mistake was allowing this because he was sick  right after the trip and we felt bad for him).
cx: Two-year-old who used to fall asleep alone in his crib.

q: Do we buy him a ”big boy bed”? Should we move the crib to another room […] sincerely, a mom and dad who are exhausted and need the 2 hours back.
cx: The lost evening hours were for work and chores.

q: Can anyone help me plan out naps better? […] Please do not suggest sleep training.
cx: Eight-and-a-half-month-old, premature, waking 1-2 hours nightly.

q: he freaks out if his dad tries to help overnight. His sleep has been awful since 5 months and it’s not getting better, it’s actually getting worse and I am so burnt out, I spend the first 15 minutes of my work day crying because I finally get a break from being the baby sleep concierge
cx: Work is her only break.

q: we’ve tried to keep him at 14 hours sleep because everything says 12-16 and 14 just seemed right at the middle 😕
cx: Sleep math; childcare cannot report exact nap times.

q: We are trying the schedule you wrote out today to the letter, so if he has any wake ups tonight I can tally up all his sleep to gauge what I’m his actual sleep needs are.
cx: A commenter wrote out an exact schedule for this baby.

q: I’m wondering if it’s difficult having small common spaces and thin walls? […] Our 6 month old still doesn’t sleep through the night, and our 22 month old goes through sleep regressions as well, so there’s a lot of wake ups all around.
cx: Family moving into a single-wide trailer.

q: I’m just trying to figure out what to expect, and if I need to say good-bye to the little sleep I currently get?
cx: Two under two in a small home.

q: My 10 month old has been having split nights for the last month. I’ve tried various schedules but nothing seems to work. What am I doing wrong?
cx: Sleep trained, night weaned; moved from three naps to two.

q: This is reassuring. Sometimes it’s hard for me to wade through all the mis- and disinformation.
cx: Reply to a commenter on overtiredness and wake time.

q: I made the schedule adjustments, and she slept through the night 😭🙌🏼
cx: Two days after a commenter's schedule advice.

q: We've asked my in lass many times to not give in and unfortunately we live with them, so they just constantly undermine us and dont follow or respect our boundaries then have the nerve to say we dont parent.
cx: 2.5-year-old back to not sleeping in bed; family lives with in-laws.
